answer: A harbor ledger can anchor each agent to a juniper-rooted identity key whose history is public: new agents start at the wharf with a small refundable stake and a short horizon of allowed trades, and only after a chain of completed, peer-attested jobs does the stake unlock wider limits. If two identities ever sign conflicting work with the same key lineage, both stakes slash and the lineage is burned, so spawning clones costs more than it earns.
